text:
Aisha: seeing a weird wave of preempts + reschedules hitting multiple AZs in us-west1, started ~09:12 UTC. lots of tiny pods getting evicted and then bounce to other racks, increased tail latency on jobs. anyone else?
Rui: yup noticed it in telemetry, eviction rate spiked ~09:10 and NVLINK errors in node metrics jumped.
Noah: can you paste the pod list? also any recent infra changes (driver/daemonset/provisioner)?
Aisha: iirc we rolled out the new nic-fix daemonset to 10% last night, but that was in eu only. nothing else obvious. obj here: `kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide | grep Pending`
Marta: pinging autoscaler logs, looks like ASG bumped 30 instances between 09:05-09:20 in us-west1-b then nodes joined with taints `gpu-reserved=true:NoSchedule` missing? weird.
Aisha: i saw some nodes without the expected taint, scheduler then tried to pack onto those and preempted older pods. could be bootstrap race where node-init didn't finish labeling before join.
deploy-bot: canary rollout `node-init-v2` failed on 2/10 hosts — rolling back to v1.
Rui: that matches. if node-init v2 changed labels/taint ordering we could get transient placement churn. can we temporarily set `preferNoSchedule` or pause preemption?
Noah: quick mitigation: add a cluster-wide pod disruption budget? not ideal. better: cordon the new nodes until node-init finishes, i can run a quick filter to find nodes with missing taints.
Marta: run `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.metadata.labels} {.spec.taints}\n'` to find mismatch. also check kubelet logs for nvlink/driver errors: `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200`
Aisha: pasted a small snippet of node describe (trimmed):
```
Name: gpu-w-usw1-b-74
Taints: <none>
Labels: topology.kubernetes.io/zone=us-west1-b, accelerator=nvidia-a100
Conditions: Ready
Events:
  Warning  EvictionThreshold  kubelet  nodefs.available is now below eviction threshold
  Warning  Kubelet  Kubelet has reported nvlink error: failed to attach device
```
Rui: nodefs eviction + nvlink error => underlying driver flakiness causes pods to OOM/evict and scheduler to reshuffle. question: why are taints missing on some nodes? bootstrap race still likely.
SRE_Oncall: i'm on it, will cordon nodes missing `gpu-reserved=true:NoSchedule` and scale down ASG joiners. also rolling back node-init-canary fully.
Noah: set `--enable-bidirectional-eviction-protection=false`? (joke) :joy: seriously though, can we add a short admission webhook to gate new nodes until node-init completes?
Marta: yes we have a webhook skeleton, low risk to enable for us-west, but takes ~15m. meanwhile SRE_Oncall mitigation timeline?
SRE_Oncall: cordon/taint enforcement in 5m, rollback finished. monitoring: eviction rate down 40% since rollback. i'll post updates.
Aisha: thanks — app teams reporting tail latency improving already :thumbsup:
Rui: followups: 1) add post-join health check that asserts taint/labels before readiness; 2) add nvlink driver health probe to node-init; 3) add telemetry alert for nodes that join without expected taint.
Marta: also file a retro for bootstrap ordering. i can own it.
Aisha: new question — cost impact: autoscaler spun up 30 instances, some evicted workloads restarted => extra GPU hours. SRE_Oncall any rough estimate?
SRE_Oncall: rough calc: 30 instances * 2h * $2.5/hr = ~$150. not huge but we'll tune ASG cooldown to avoid reactive scale-ups on noisy join.
Noah: will follow up with a scheduler change PR to prefer nodes with `gpu-reserved` label for new scheduling decisions to reduce preempt churn.
Marta: 👍 filing thread and adding links to logs + kube events in the incident doc.
Aisha: thanks everyone. tagging folks who saw user impact: @eng-support and @customersuccess.
deploy-bot: rollback `node-init-v2` completed at 09:37 UTC (canary halted).
